acls.notEnabledTitle: ACL authorization is not enabled on this cluster
acls.notEnabled: ACLs (Access Control Lists) restrict who may read or write which topics. This broker has no authorizer configured, so permission rules cannot be viewed or managed — this is the cluster's security state, not a software fault. To enable: ① configure authorizer.class and super.users in the broker's server.properties and restart it; ② switch the connection to SASL authentication; ③ reopen this page to manage rules.
config.addHint: Type a config name, fuzzy search supported
config.revertHint: Restore cluster default (clears this topic's override on save)
share.empty: No share groups (requires Kafka 4.2+ with group.share.enable=true)
share.hint: Share groups (KIP-932): multiple consumers share reading the same records; the broker tracks delivery. Requires Kafka 4.2+.
share.unsupported: This cluster does not support Share Groups. Requires: 1) Kafka 4.2+ brokers; 2) group.share.enable=true in server.properties, then restart.
share.clearHint: Pick the topics whose delivery progress to forget. The group restarts delivery from the beginning on them. Irreversible.
share.alterHint: Records at or before the start offset count as delivered and will not be handed to this group again. The broker rejects alters while the group is actively consuming.
share.activeWarn: This share group has active members; the broker may reject the alter (group must be Empty).
share.invalidOffset: Start offset must be a non-negative integer
share.offsetsEmpty: No offset records (empty after clearing; reappears once share consumers start)
error.refused.hint: Verify the broker address and port|Make sure the broker is running|Check the server firewall or cloud security group for the port|If the address is correct, check the broker's advertised.listeners
error.timeout.hint: Check that the broker is reachable from this machine|Check the cloud security group or firewall for the port|If connecting over the public internet, rule out VPN or proxy interference
error.dns.hint: Verify the broker address spelling|Make sure the host name resolves locally (try the IP instead)
error.tls.hint: Confirm the port actually uses TLS|Enable TLS in the connection settings|Self-signed certificates must be trusted by this machine
error.auth.hint: Verify the username and password|Match the SASL mechanism (PLAIN/SCRAM etc.) to the broker config|Make sure authentication is enabled in the connection settings
error.denied.hint: The account lacks authorization for this resource|Ask an administrator to add the ACL
error.coordinator.hint: Brokers are electing a leader or moving the coordinator|Retry in a few seconds
error.rebalance.hint: A member is joining or leaving, triggering a rebalance|Retry shortly
error.unsupportedVersion: Broker version does not support this feature
error.unsupportedVersion.hint: This feature requires a newer Kafka broker|Check the cluster's broker version first
error.groupNotEmpty.hint: Active members block this administrative operation|Wait for members to leave (or stop the consumers) and retry
error.groupMissing.hint: The group was deleted, or never existed|Refresh to see the current group list
error.shareUnsupported: This cluster does not support Share Groups
error.shareUnsupported.hint: Requires Kafka 4.2+ with group.share.enable=true|Upgrade the cluster and restart the brokers
error.conflict.hint: A resource with this name exists|Pick a different name

error.generic.hint: Expand the details for the exact cause|If it keeps failing, refresh or reopen the page

acls.emptyDesc: No ACL rules exist yet. If the cluster has no authorizer configured, this page stays empty and permissions cannot be managed.
acls.emptySteps: Configure authorizer.class and super.users in the broker's server.properties, then restart the broker|Connect with SASL (PLAINTEXT connections cannot manage ACLs)|Reopen this page to manage rules

topics.internalDeleteBlocked: {0} is a Kafka internal topic (consumer offsets / share-group state). Deleting it would wipe every consumer group's offsets, so deletion is blocked here.
topics.internalHint: Kafka-reserved topic: carries cluster-critical state (consumer offsets / share-group state). Browsing and export stay available; writes and deletes are protected.
topics.internalToolbarNote: Reserved topic: produce / import / delete records are blocked
topics.internalConfigNote: Reserved topic: config managed by Kafka, editing locked
topics.ecosystemDeleteBlocked: "{0}" is managed by an external service (e.g. Schema Registry / Kafka Connect) and holds that service's critical data — deleting it would wipe the service's data, so deletion is blocked here. To clean it up, use the service's own API instead.
topics.ecosystemHint: Managed by an external service (Schema Registry / Kafka Connect, …): carries that service's critical data (schema registrations, connector progress). Browsing and export stay available; writes and deletes are protected.
topics.protectedHint: Protected topic (Kafka-reserved or service-managed): browsing and export stay available; writes and deletes are protected.
topics.protectedToolbarNote: Protected topic: produce / import / delete records are blocked
topics.protectedConfigNote: Protected topic: config managed by the owning system, editing locked
conn.cloneConfirm: Clone connection {0}? Creates a new connection using the same config (with a copied password).
conn.saveReconnectHint: Saving drops this connection's open session; the next use reconnects with the new config.

decode.confluentHint: This value looks Confluent-wrapped (schema id {0}). Configure a Registry on the Schema Registry page, re-browse with 解码 checked, and it will decode automatically.
acls.intro: ACLs (Access Control Lists) decide WHO can do WHAT to WHICH resources. Rules take effect immediately; DENY wins over ALLOW.
acls.fieldDesc.principal: Principal — the user being granted, format User:<name> (the SASL username)
acls.fieldDesc.resourceName: Resource name — topic name for TOPIC, group id for GROUP; with PREFIXED, a prefix
acls.fieldDesc.host: Host — the client connection address; * means any host
acls.opDesc.ANY: Matches any operation (query filter only — do not create rules with it)
acls.opDesc.CREATE: Create — create topics, partitions and similar resources
acls.opDesc.DELETE: Delete — delete topics, records and similar resources
acls.opDesc.DESCRIBE: Describe — list and view metadata (not configs)
acls.opDesc.ALTER_CONFIGS: Alter configs — dynamically change topic/broker configs
acls.opDesc.CLUSTER_ACTION: Cluster action — required for internal coordination (controlled shutdown)
acls.resDesc.TOPIC: Topic — the message stream, the most common target
acls.resDesc.GROUP: Consumer group — controls who can join and consume
acls.resDesc.CLUSTER: Cluster — cluster-level operations (create topics, controlled shutdown)
acls.resDesc.TRANSACTIONAL_ID: Transactional ID — authorization target of transactional producers
acls.resDesc.USER: User — used when managing delegation tokens
acls.patDesc.LITERAL: Literal — matches resources whose name is exactly equal
acls.patDesc.PREFIXED: Prefixed — matches every resource starting with the name (app- covers app-a, app-b)
topic.partitionsHint: Parallelism — how many consumers can read this topic concurrently; scale as needed
topic.rfHint: Replication Factor — how many copies of each partition are kept for fault tolerance; single-broker clusters must use 1

quotas.intro: Quotas throttle clients per entity (e.g. produce bandwidth for one Client ID). The broker API is upsert — setting a value on a new entity creates the entry. 0 forbids the operation entirely.
